text:
Maria: Observed a regression on staging where KV mem growth spikes for longctx workloads after the kernel-selection change. Repro script: `./run_longctx_workload --profile --seed=42`
Kevin: saw that too. pprof heap diff shows ~3.8MB growth per 1000 tokens, looks like pinned pages from fragmented slabs.
Sachin: do we have a concrete trace? where is the time spent?
Maria: attaching quick profiler summary from last run: `pprof -http=:8080 heap.diff` — hot path is `kv_cache::prefix_lookup` + memcpy in `alloc::alloc` when rehydrating pages.
Eva: hmm, could be our prefetch that allocates whole page buffers then never releases due to session-stickiness keys preventing eviction.
Kevin: I think the root cause is keying. We're using a composite key: `tenant|sessionid|prefix-fingerprint|epoch` which prevents cross-request reuse and fragments the hotset. Example: `kvkey:v2:tid=acme:sid=3c7f:fp=0x9a1b:e=42`
Sachin: that matches. If sessionid is high-cardinality, we lose reuse and the LRU heuristics keep many small entries -> fragmentation.
Maria: Profiling notes: after kernel-selection PR #3124 we started larger batch sizes and the runtime kept prefixes in memory longer (to avoid rehydration latency), but when a tenant has many sessions that defeats the cache. Net effect: more pinned pages + more memcpy when reusing.
Eva: Reproduction steps I used: `env REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=1 REDWOOD_BATCH_MAX=64 ./run_longctx_workload --tenant=acme --sessions=500` — you can see memory climb steadily.
Kevin: Proposed short-term mitigation: strip `sessionid` out of the canonical cache key for prefix-only entries and include `sessionid` only for session-scoped ephemeral entries. That lets prefix entries be shared across sessions and reduces fragmentation.
Sachin: Agree. Also think we should add a compact-on-evict background task to collapse small allocations into free slabs; fragmentation is the main issue.
Maria: Long-term: consider two-layer keying: (1) global prefix key hashed by tenant+prefix-fp, (2) session overlay for ephemeral deltas. Routing will consult overlay first then global.
Eva: Quick implementation sketch: change key schema to `pfx:v3:tid=<tid>:fp=<fp>` (global) and `sess:v1:tid=<tid>:sid=<sid>:fp=<fp>` (session overlay). Keep eviction TTLs different: global TTL > session TTL.
Kevin: We'll need migration logic to migrate existing entries or accept cold misses for a short window. Also update Console counters to show global vs session residency.
Sachin: Also saw an odd interaction with kernel selection: bigger batches amplified the reuse penalty because more queries hit slightly different prefixes concurrently, creating many near-duplicate cache entries. Could add a prefix-normalization step before keying (trim trailing punctuation, collapse whitespace).
Maria: Agreed. Action items: 1) Kevin + Sachin: implement key change + normalization in a small PR, add feature flag `kv_key_v3` (ETA EOD tomorrow). 2) Eva: add compaction sweeper to background jobs and a short smoke test for fragmentation reduction (ETA 2d). 3) Maria: run longctx perf harness against kernel-selection branch with the new flags and report heap diffs.
Kevin: I'll open the PR and add tests for cross-session reuse.
Sachin: I'll add a microbenchmark that simulates 10k sessions with shared prefixes to compare resident set and lookup latency.
kv-bot: compaction-job scheduled for 1733339000 on staging (no-downtime). :eyes:
Eva: One more note — paging behavior. When pages get evicted we saw a surge of disk I/O on some Dedicated nodes because we fall back to compressed backing store. We should prefer in-memory eviction (LRU slab reclamation) over flushing to disk during steady-state. Will add config knob.
Maria: Thanks team. If we can get the key migration behind a flag we can measure impact on perf/regressions without customer-facing changes.
Kevin: thumbs-up. I'll include telemetry to measure prefix reuse rate and median mem per-1000-tokens.
Maria: Great. If anyone finds a quick win add it to the PR checklist. :thumbsup:
